ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The q(t) given in the figure is a train of triangular sampling pulses periodically repeated along the time axis; the peak value of each triangular pulse is 1. The pulse centered at t=0 falls to 0 at t=-\tau and t=\tau, so the pulse half-width is \tau. The figure also marks the period of adjacent pulses of the same shape as T=1/(2f_m). Reasoning: Take the reference triangular pulse within one period as q_0(t)=1-|t|/\tau, |t|\le \tau; otherwise q_0(t)=0. The Fourier series of the periodic signal q(t) is written as q(t)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} c_n e^{jn\omega_0 t}, where \omega_0=2\pi/T. Its coefficient is c_n=(1/T)\int_{-\tau}^{\tau}(1-|t|/\tau)e^{-jn\omega_0 t}dt. The Fourier transform of the triangular pulse gives c_n=(\tau/T)\mathrm{Sa}^2(n\omega_0\tau/2), where \mathrm{Sa}(x)=\sin x/x. From T=1/(2f_m) in the figure, obtain \omega_0=2\pi/T=4\pi f_m, therefore c_n=(\tau/T)\mathrm{Sa}^2(2\pi n\tau f_m). The sampled signal is m_s(t)=m(t)q(t), and multiplication in the time domain corresponds to modulating m(t) with each Fourier-series exponential term of q(t), so in the frequency domain periodic shifted copies of M(\omega) are obtained: M_s(\omega)=\sum_n c_n M(\omega-n\omega_0). Substituting c_n and \omega_0 then gives the required spectrum.

再推理：令 q(t) 为 p(t) 以周期 T 重复得到的周期信号，即 q(t)=\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}p(t-kT)。对单位高度、半宽为 \tau 的三角脉冲，有连续时间傅里叶变换 P(\omega)=\tau\,\mathrm{Sa}^2(\omega\tau/2)。周期重复信号的基波角频率为 \omega_0=2\pi/T。由图中 T=1/(2f_m)，所以 \omega_0=4\pi f_m。周期信号 q(t) 的频谱在 \omega=n\omega_0 处为冲激线谱，其权重与 P(n\omega_0)/T 成正比。采样信号为 m_s(t)=m(t)q(t)，时域相乘对应频域卷积，因此得到 M(\omega) 的加权平移副本：M_s(\omega)=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}P(n\omega_0)M(\omega-n\omega_0)。代入 P(n\omega_0)=\tau\mathrm{Sa}^2(n\omega_0\tau/2) 以及 \omega_0=4\pi f_m，可得 n\omega_0\tau/2=2\pi n\tau f_m。因此 sampled signal 的频谱为 M_s(\omega)=\frac{\tau}{T}\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}\mathrm{Sa}^2(2\pi n\tau f_m)M(\omega-4\pi n f_m)。

raw_record.original_question: The maximum frequency of the signal \( m(t) \) is less than \( f_{\mathrm{m}} \). If \( m(t) \) is sampled using \( q(t) \) as shown in the image, determine the expression for the spectrum of the sampled signal.
raw_record.answer: \( M_{\mathrm{s}}(\omega) = \frac{\tau}{T} \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} \text{Sa}^2\left(2 \pi n \tau f_{\mathrm{m}}\right) M\left(\omega - 4\pi n f_{\mathrm{m}}\right) \)
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The q(t) given in the figure is a train of triangular sampling pulses periodically repeated along the time axis; the peak value of each triangular pulse is 1. The pulse centered at t=0 falls to 0 at t=-\tau and t=\tau, so the pulse half-width is \tau. The figure also marks the period of adjacent pulses of the same shape as T=1/(2f_m).
Reasoning: Take the reference triangular pulse within one period as q_0(t)=1-|t|/\tau, |t|\le \tau; otherwise q_0(t)=0. The Fourier series of the periodic signal q(t) is written as q(t)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} c_n e^{jn\omega_0 t}, where \omega_0=2\pi/T. Its coefficient is c_n=(1/T)\int_{-\tau}^{\tau}(1-|t|/\tau)e^{-jn\omega_0 t}dt. The Fourier transform of the triangular pulse gives c_n=(\tau/T)\mathrm{Sa}^2(n\omega_0\tau/2), where \mathrm{Sa}(x)=\sin x/x. From T=1/(2f_m) in the figure, obtain \omega_0=2\pi/T=4\pi f_m, therefore c_n=(\tau/T)\mathrm{Sa}^2(2\pi n\tau f_m). The sampled signal is m_s(t)=m(t)q(t), and multiplication in the time domain corresponds to modulating m(t) with each Fourier-series exponential term of q(t), so in the frequency domain periodic shifted copies of M(\omega) are obtained: M_s(\omega)=\sum_n c_n M(\omega-n\omega_0). Substituting c_n and \omega_0 then gives the required spectrum.
